prompt: Mid-case: The client's profit fell 20%. You've found that revenue is flat and that COGS rose 25% because bean prices doubled. You also learned the client opened two stores in 2019. You haven't looked at labor costs yet. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: revenue is flat and COGS rose 25% on doubled bean prices, which fully explains the drop, so labor doesn't need checking.
options.feedback: It closes a question that's still open: labor hasn't been checked.

options.text: So far: revenue fell and bean prices doubled, pushing COGS up 25%. Labor costs come next.
options.feedback: It misstates what you found: revenue is flat, not falling.

options.text: So far: revenue is flat, and profit fell mainly because bean prices doubled, pushing COGS up 25%. Labor comes next.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open.

options.text: So far: revenue is flat, COGS rose 25% on doubled bean prices, and the client opened two stores in 2019. Next, labor.
options.feedback: The 2019 stores don't explain this year's drop, so they don't belong in the summary.

explanation: Known: revenue is flat and COGS rose 25% because bean prices doubled. Suspected: bean prices explain most of the 20% profit drop. Next: check labor costs. If labor also rose sharply, it shares the blame.

irrelevant_facts: The client opened two stores in 2019.
